params.body:
I went looking for a bug that was not there, and found the one that matters.

The claim was that the queue worker's PATH lacks the Claude CLI, so the look-further pass never runs. The worker's PATH does lack it, but `LookFurther` prepends `~/.npm-global/bin` itself, and the record says the pass has run: six drops reached stage `looked` on 10 and 11 September with nothing in the log. Nothing was silently skipped.

What is true is that Vera cannot say whether that pass *could* run. The step needs a model, and a login that expired or an account out of budget fails in the quietest way there is: the step says so and stops, the review stays at its first catch, and nothing anywhere says why. That fault ran unnoticed for months, twice, on the Signal Observatory, which is why `pipeline-check` exists there.

So Vera says it herself and Elixir reads it, through the module's own `extra` door:

- `App\Elixir\AgentProbe` reports whether a token is configured, whether the CLI is where the job will look for it, and what the last pass did.
- `LookFurther` records the outcome of each pass, including the first line of the failure, so "failed: You have hit your weekly limit" is a fact in the health answer rather than a silence.
- The probe never calls a model. A health check that spends the budget it is watching is its own outage.

The test pins both halves: no token configured is reported as a fact, and a failed pass carries why it failed. Suite 47/47.
params.title: Of de agent kon lopen, is een feit en geen stilte
